road.name: The Toll of Empty Wagons
road.threat: Armed extortion and a trapped causeway. A rope or climbing kit can open a side approach.
road.brief: Three wagons carrying winter seed have stopped answering their road signals. Find the missing drivers before the village’s planting stores are sold across the border.

opening.narrate: Reeve Aveline gave you this job in the square with a list. Three wagons of winter seed, three drivers, and one of the drivers Jory Tanner, whose family has farmed the Ashford road since before the bell. 'If that seed is sold across the border,' she said, 'we eat the seed corn in February and go hungry in May. Bring it back. Bring Jory back first.'

Now an empty wagon stands on the western road with its wheels chocked, not broken. Somebody stopped it on purpose, took the horses and left the seed. From the tollhouse beyond, where the new toll captain, Venn, keeps his office, a bell repeats three short notes: the old road signal for 'wait', rung backwards.

opening.text: Wagon's chocked. Bandits don't chock wheels.
Clerks do.

opening.narrate: A face appears behind a shutter in the tollhouse yard, sees you, flashes one hand, and is pulled away from the glass.

road.clue: The road signal has been reversed. Drivers are being held while their cargo is inventoried; the toll captain’s own payment slips contradict his orders.

investigate.label: Compare the wagon manifest with the toll notices

success.narrate: The manifest says three wagons, forty sacks each. Venn's notice on the tollhouse door says the seed is 'held for inspection'. The two papers carry two different seals: the road wardens' thorn, and a second one that Venn has had cut for himself, slightly crooked.

success.text: He's collecting the toll twice. Once for the road. Once for himself.

success.narrate: Tucked behind the notice is a pay-slip in Venn's own hand, for 'yard work', to three men whose faces are on the wanted board in Ashford.

failure.narrate: The handwriting defeats you. But scratched into the abandoned wagon's tailboard with a nail is a tally: three strokes, and the word ALIVE.

failure.text: Jory Tanner's hand. He keeps the tithe-book at the shrine. Nobody else makes an A like a tent.

route.label: Cross under the causeway and reach the drivers

success.narrate: Under the causeway the old drainage arches are knee-deep and full of frogs. You come up through a grating in the drivers' yard, where Jory Tanner is sitting on a seed sack with his hands tied, and he looks at you as if you are late for supper.

success.text: Took your time. Here. Venn makes everybody sign for everything. These are his copies.

success.narrate: He has been sitting on the duplicate receipts for two days.

route.failure: A loose stone gives you away. You reach the tollhouse, but the captain pulls his guards inward.

crisis.narrate: Captain Venn offers to release the wagons if you leave the documents. The drivers watch his hands; one rests on a signal cord leading toward their locked yard.
Captain Venn offers to release the wagons if you turn round now and forget you ever saw his yard. The drivers watch his hands; one rests on a signal cord leading toward their locked yard.

peaceful.label: Use the duplicate receipts to make the guards stand down

success.narrate: The guards read what they have been paid to enforce. One cuts the yard lock; the captain surrenders his keys without a fight.

You don't have the captain's papers, so you ask the drivers instead, loudly, in front of his guards: how long they have been held, what has been taken off their carts, and who signed for it. The guards have families on this road too. By the third answer one of them cuts the yard lock, and the captain surrenders his keys without a fight.

peaceful.failure: Venn calls the receipts stolen and signals the yard guard. His hesitation gives you a chance to reach the lock before the drivers are moved.
peaceful.labelNoLead: Ask the drivers, in front of the guards, what they are being held for

objective.name: Release the wagon drivers
objective.label: Break the yard lock
objective.description: Two successful actions release the drivers and end the encounter without needing to defeat every guard.
objective.failText: Venn moves part of the stolen cargo. The seed shortage will persist, and the drivers still need a way out.
objective.successText: The drivers escape with their wagons; the remaining guards abandon the tollhouse.

after.narrate: The drivers get their horses back from a field behind the tollhouse, where Venn had been charging them for grazing. Jory Tanner counts the seed sacks twice, and then a third time, out loud, because his boy Wat is watching from the milestone.

after.text: Forty, forty, thirty-nine. One's gone. Venn's guards took it for their own fields, I'd bet. Let them have it. I've got my wagons and my boy.

after.narrate: Venn's strongbox holds the illegal tolls, sorted by road and by week. It could go back to the households it was taken from, or pay for an escort on this road so it doesn't happen again.

decisions.label: Return the illegal tolls to the drivers

text.narrate: You count the toll money back out to the drivers, family by family and week by week, with Venn's own ledger as the list. It takes all afternoon. Jory Tanner tells everyone in three villages.

text.text: That is the slowest way to give money back I've ever seen.
It's the only way they'll believe it.

decisions.label: Fund a permanent caravan escort

text.narrate: You hand Venn's strongbox to Reeve Aveline, who uses it to hire four riders to keep the western road through the winter. The trading houses in Ashford have heard about it before you get there.

text.text: Next time somebody tries this, there's somebody to stop them.
And the families who paid Venn get a road instead of their money.

road.approach: The causeway runs straight at the tollhouse, in full view of its shutters. Underneath it, the old drainage arches lead toward the drivers’ yard: low, wet and out of sight.

talks.label: Read the new toll board at the foot of the causeway

lines.narrate: The toll board has been repainted this month. The old board charged a penny a wheel. The new one charges a penny a wheel, a penny a hoof, two pence a sack, a road-keeping levy, a bell levy (the bell has been silent for a week), and a fee for the reading of this board.

lines.text: That last one's new.
He's charging people to find out what he's charging them.

lines.narrate: Under the board, in chalk, somebody has written VENN IS A THIEF. Somebody else has rubbed it out, though not very hard.

talks.label: Talk to the boy sitting on the milestone

lines.narrate: A boy of about twelve is sitting on the milestone with his boots off, rubbing his feet. He has the Tanner chin.

lines.text: Pa said if they stopped us, I was to run home and not look back. I ran. I'm a good runner. He said that too.
I came back, though. Somebody has to be here when he comes out.
Stay on the stone. If you see us run, run too.
Which way?
Same way as us. Faster.

marsh.name: Bitter Water at Fenmere
marsh.threat: Poisoned water and flooded paths, and two banks of one village ready to fight over it. Antitoxin protects the next poison save; a lantern helps you find the safe valves.
marsh.brief: Fenmere's well has turned bitter. The upper bank blames the marsh gatherers on the lower bank, who blame the new sluice-house the upper bank built. Find the cause before fear becomes violence.

opening.narrate: Fenmere is two villages pretending to be one: the upper bank on its rise, with the well and the church, and the lower bank down among the reeds, where the gatherers cut rushes and smoke eels. Between them stands the new sluice-house, which the upper bank paid for and the lower bank did not ask for.

Reeds lie flat around it. A sick heron watches from a dry pipe. On the upper bank, villagers stand holding pitchforks they are pretending are for hay. On the lower bank, the gatherers hold eel-spears behind their headwoman, old Sefa, and are not pretending anything.
On the sluice-house steps in the middle, a young woman with a little bell on a cord round her neck is trying to make both sides listen to her, and neither is.

opening.text: I'm the keeper! It's the ward's water! If everybody would just... Nobody poisoned anybody!

opening.narrate: At the edge of it all, a white-haired woman with a brown goat on a rope watches the whole thing and says nothing at all.

marsh.clue: The new sluice draws dissolved ward ash from a cracked jar dumped upstream. Both banks drink the same tainted water; neither poisoned the other.

investigate.label: Examine the residue in the sluice with the village healers

success.narrate: The residue in the sluice's intake is copper-green and smells like a burnt church. Ward ash. Somebody has dumped old ward ash upstream in a cracked jar, and the new sluice draws it in and sends it straight up to the well.

success.text: Ward ash? Nobody in Fenmere burns wards.
Nobody in Fenmere. Somebody upstream is getting rid of something.

failure.narrate: Your samples spoil in the jar. But the sick fish are all lying below the new sluice, belly-up, in a line that points straight at it.

failure.text: Told you.

route.label: Reach the intake through the vapor trench
route.success: You choose the dry stepping stones and arrive without disturbing the trapped vapor.
route.failure: A gas pocket ruptures around the party. You reach the intake coughing, with less time to work.

crisis.narrate: As you reach the valves, the water in the sluice-race stands up. It is the fen's guardian, the old ward-spirit of the marsh, choked on the ash and lashing at anything that comes near the valves.

crisis.text: Open the spillway and the lower bank's shelters flood! Leave it shut and the well's poisoned again! I don't... I haven't got a verse for this!
Then we make you some room to find one.

peaceful.label: Show both banks the residue and organise a controlled release

success.narrate: You stand on the sluice-house steps with a jar of green water in each hand and make both banks look at it. Then you make them look at each other, which is harder.

It is Sefa who moves first. She sends her grandsons up to help carry the upper bank's old people to the high ground, and the upper bank, ashamed of itself, sends carts down for the gatherers' sick. With nobody left inside its boundary, the guardian lets Ilka sing it back to sleep.

success.text: I did have a verse. It was the second one. It's always the second one.

peaceful.failure: The warning gets some people moving, but the keeper cannot calm the guardian. You must open the safe valves while it rages.
peaceful.labelNoLead: Get both banks to look at the water together and organize a controlled release

objective.name: Vent the poisoned intake
objective.label: Turn a safe intake valve
objective.description: Three successful actions purge the poison and release the guardian. Antitoxin protects against the trench, not physical attacks.
objective.failText: The emergency spill floods some shelters. Stop the danger to prevent further losses; the flooded homes will need repair.
objective.successText: Clean water replaces the bitter flow; the guardian’s bindings dissolve.

after.narrate: By evening the water runs clean, and the two banks are standing on either side of the sluice-house arguing about who will look after it, which everyone agrees is an improvement.

after.text: Somebody has to keep the sluice. It can't be me. I've got the ward.

after.narrate: The woman with the goat comes down from the rise at last, looks at the sluice-house, looks at both banks, and goes home again without a word. Ilka says that was Brannagh, and that it means she approves.

decisions.label: Establish a shared water council

text.narrate: Each side appoints a keeper for the water. The gatherers send Sefa. The village sends Brannagh, who says she'll do it as long as nobody expects her to be pleasant. The first meeting lasts four hours. At the end of it, the water is still clean.

decisions.label: Ask Ashford's engineers to maintain the sluice

text.narrate: Paid engineers from Ashford take charge of the sluice and promise an inspection every month. They send Fenmere the first bill before they have left the village.

marsh.approach: A trench of yellow vapor runs under the reeds to the intake. The causeway above it is dry and open, and both banks are watching it.

talks.label: Talk to Ilka, the young keeper

lines.text: I've been keeper since the spring. Old Edric kept the ward before me, and then he went off to Ashford about some letters and never came back, and they gave it to me because I know the verses. I'm good at the verses. I'm not good at this.
The well went bitter the week the sluice-house opened. The upper bank says the gatherers put something in it. The gatherers say the sluice did it. Nobody asks the keeper. I'm nineteen.
Edric Moss?

lines.narrate: Maren takes out a soft, much-folded sheet of paper, runs her finger down it, and stops. She does not say anything else. She puts the paper away very carefully.

talks.label: Ask the gatherers' headwoman what she thinks happened

lines.narrate: Old Sefa is smoking eels on the lower bank as if nothing at all were happening, which on the lower bank is a political position.

lines.text: The upper bank built a sluice on our water to fill their well faster. Then their well went bad. And now it's us that poisoned it. Funny how it's always us.
Did you?
If I poisoned somebody, soldier, they'd know about it.

bridge.name: The Last Cart over Ashford
bridge.threat: Sabotaged anchors and barricades. Climbing gear helps cross; protecting refugees matters more than chasing every raider.
bridge.brief: Refugees are trapped beyond the western bridge. Orin recognizes the banners of the company holding it. Get the last carts across before a demolition charge is lit.

opening.narrate: Ashford's western span is the only bridge in thirty miles a loaded cart can cross. A bell on the gatehouse sounds once for each cart allowed through. It stopped ringing an hour ago.

On the far bank, people from the burned villages wait with everything they own on carts. Between them and the bridge, a company of soldiers holds the far gate, under a banner that stops Orin in the middle of the road.

opening.text: Second Company. My old company.
Is that good?
Ask me in an hour.

opening.narrate: Under the span, freshly cut cables sway over the river.

bridge.clue: The demolition order is forged. A faction within the bridge company intends to abandon both refugees and its own rear guard.

investigate.label: Ask the bridge veterans to compare their orders

success.narrate: The veterans let you see the demolition order. Orin holds it up to the light.

success.text: That's Colonel Ashe's signature. Colonel Ashe died at Calder. I carried him.

success.narrate: The paper goes from hand to hand down the line, and you watch them work it out, one by one: somebody forged an order to blow the bridge with the rear guard still on it.

investigate.failure: The veterans close ranks. One quietly warns you that the demolition fuse is already laid beneath the guardhouse.

route.label: Cross the maintenance anchors to the far gate
route.success: You reach the fuse box unseen and disconnect the first charge.
route.failure: An anchor tears loose. You reach the far bank bruised, while the sentries call their lieutenant.

crisis.narrate: Lieutenant Hal holds the gate: a small, hard woman with a voice that carries across a river.

crisis.text: Nobody else crosses. The span goes at the bell. Those are my orders.
Hal.
Stoneward.

crisis.narrate: Neither of them says anything else. Behind Hal, a girl of eight or so in the last cart leans out and asks Orin whether soldiers always leave first.

peaceful.label: Offer the soldiers a shared withdrawal with the refugees

success.narrate: You don't argue with Hal. You show her the order with a dead man's name on it. Then you ask her what she did at Calder, the crossing where their company left people behind.
Hal looks at Orin for a long moment. Then she turns and bellows down the span: every cart onto the bridge, the company to march out behind them, nobody left behind as a diversion.

success.text: If somebody wants this bridge blown, they can do it with me standing on it.

peaceful.failure: Most soldiers hesitate, but the demolition crew follows its own orders. You must clear the cart route under fire.

objective.name: Escort the final refugee carts
objective.label: Open a lane for a refugee cart
objective.description: Three successful actions secure the evacuation. Companions hold the demolition crew away from you.
objective.failText: One loaded supply cart is lost to the river. The remaining people still need a crossing, and Highpass will receive fewer blankets and tools.
objective.successText: The last cart reaches the near bank; the demolition crew has nothing left to hold hostage.

after.narrate: The last cart rolls off the span. The demolition crew sits in a row on the bank with their hands on their heads, looking more embarrassed than dangerous. Most of them are boys who did what the paper said.

after.text: So. Make an example of them, or put them to work? The paper says example. I'm off papers today.

decisions.label: Offer supervised repair work instead of punishment

text.narrate: The demolition crew will spend the next month re-hanging the cables they cut, beside the refugees they nearly drowned. Tonight, for the first time, they eat at the same fire.

text.text: I'd have had them in front of a tribunal. Maybe I'd have been wrong. Ask me in a year.

decisions.label: Preserve the orders and call a public tribunal

text.narrate: The forged order goes into Ashford's public record. Quartermaster Iona reads it into the minutes herself, every word, including the dead colonel's name, and Ashford's council has to answer for whoever sent it.

text.text: Slow. But nobody gets to say it didn't happen.

bridge.approach: The maintenance anchors hang under the span, slick with river spray. On the deck above, the queue of carts waits in plain sight of Hal’s line.

talks.label: Ask Orin about the Second Company

lines.text: Eight years ago we held a ford at Calder for a column of farmers coming down out of the hills. Orders came to fall back. We fell back. The farmers didn't know we'd gone until they reached the water.
Hal was a corporal then. She went back for them on her own and got eleven of them out. They gave her a reprimand and a stripe in the same week.
I didn't go back.

archive.name: Letters from the Drowned Archive
archive.threat: Rising water, undead wardens and fragile records. A lantern helps navigation; holy water or radiant weapons affect the undead.
archive.brief: Maren’s missing shrine keepers sent their last letters here. Find the archive’s ward diagram and recover what remains before the reservoir rises again.

opening.narrate: The drowned archive was the wardens' record-house once, built into the side of the reservoir. Then the dam was raised, and now the water comes into it every season and goes out again a little slower each time.

Desks drift at the foot of a flooded stair. Above them, a grey figure in an archivist's sleeves goes on sorting ruined pages into dry drawers that are not there any more, one page at a time, very carefully.

opening.text: Six of my keepers sent their last letters here. If they're anywhere, they're in those drawers.
And if the water comes up while we're looking?
Then we look faster.

archive.clue: The ward network was built as a council of independent voices. A single central command would bind every keeper as Sable tried to bind the bell spirit.

investigate.label: Read the surviving correspondence with Maren

success.narrate: Maren reads the letters aloud by lantern-light, one after another, the way you read names at a funeral: slowly, so nobody is skipped.

Between them they show you two things. The ward network was built on purpose as a council of separate voices, each keeper answerable to their own village. And the keystone that ties it together was sent up to Highpass, which is exactly what anybody wanting one voice would need.

failure.narrate: Most of the ink has run to nothing. But Maren finds the dispatch mark on the last bundle, the same on every letter: all of them were sent on to Highpass.

failure.text: They were writing to somebody up there. Somebody who never answered.

route.label: Navigate the flooded stacks without breaking the seals

success.narrate: You find the archivists' service stair behind a fallen shelf and go up it in single file, with the water lapping one step behind you. The dry alcoves on the way are still sealed. Orin closes each one again after you pass, as if somebody might come back for them.

route.failure: A shelf collapses beneath you. You reach the central record chamber with water rising behind your boots.

crisis.narrate: The record chamber is the one dry room in the building. The archivist stands in front of the diagram cabinet with its arms spread, the way a clerk stands in front of a counter at closing time.

crisis.text: Every keeper is to be accounted for before the record is closed. Every keeper. I cannot close the drawer. I have been trying for six years.

crisis.narrate: Some of the keepers in its drawers never came back. Destroying the archivist would be easier than admitting that. It would also be quicker, and the water is still rising.

peaceful.label: Read the keepers’ names and acknowledge the unfinished record

success.narrate: You don't fight the archivist. You help it finish.

Maren reads the names from her list, and you read the names from its drawers, and between you, for every one, you say what happened: delivered, buried, lost, unknown. The archivist writes each answer down in a hand that leaves no ink.

success.text: Anwen Holt. Lowmere. No last letter.
No. There isn't one.
Then she is not finished either.

success.narrate: It stops sorting. It gathers the last letters out of the one dry drawer and holds them out, not to you, but to Maren. Then it opens the diagram cabinet and steps aside.

peaceful.failure: The unfinished names catch in the ward. The archivist turns hostile, but the cabinet remains close enough to reach.

objective.name: Recover the diagram and last letters
objective.label: Preserve a sealed record drawer
objective.description: Three successful actions recover the essential records and end the binding. Killing enemies is not required.
objective.failText: Some personal letters dissolve before they can be sealed. The diagram and remaining names still need to be recovered.
objective.successText: The sealed drawers float free; the archivist is released from its impossible duty.

after.narrate: The diagram is safe in its oilcloth. Maren has the keepers’ letters, a damp bundle tied with archive string, and she has stopped at the one on top.

after.text: Brother Edric Moss. He kept the well-ward at Fenmere. To his sister Hesper, at the dyers’ yard in Highpass.
You knew him.
He owed me two candles and an apology. He would have paid the candles.

after.narrate: She puts the letter inside her coat, next to her list.
The diagram could be published for everyone who tends a ward, or kept under council protection while the sabotage is investigated.

decisions.label: Share the diagram with local ward keepers
decisions.text: Knowledge spreads beyond a single council. The keepers can prepare their own defenses.

decisions.label: Give the original to a guarded public archive
decisions.text: The council establishes a protected record, with named witnesses for every copy.

archive.approach: The flooded stacks run in long aisles toward the record chamber. Some shelves still hold their seals, and one wrong step brings a whole wall of them down. The main stair is clear, loud, and in full view.

talks.label: Ask Maren about her list

lines.narrate: Maren takes out a single sheet of paper, folded so often it has gone soft as cloth.

lines.text: When Central Command took the wards, the shrine keepers who said no went missing. Not all at once. One a season, so nobody would notice. These are the ones I trained with, or knew, or owed something.
I don't expect to find them alive. I'd like to find out where they stopped. People should know where to put the flowers.
How many?
Nineteen. Fourteen when I started writing them down. I keep adding.

signal.name: A Light above the Storm
signal.threat: Charged ward machinery and exposed climbing. A Storm Grounder opens a protected approach; a climbing kit aids the ascent.
signal.brief: The tower above Highpass repeats a distress signal in Nessa’s old code. Restore its beacon before the mountain caravans enter the storm blind.

opening.narrate: Highpass Watch sits across the top of the pass like a cork in a bottle, and every refugee from the high villages has come up against it this year. Its captain has found room for all of them. She has not found room for anything else.

Above the fort, the old signal tower is flashing a distress code into a sky full of lightning. The bolts crawl sideways along its bronze rings instead of coming down. Someone has tied a scout's scarf round the lowest signal arm, where nobody on the road can see it.

opening.text: That's my scarf. That's Wren's code. That's... she's up there.

signal.clue: The tower is broadcasting a warning, not summoning the storm. Its keeper diverted the lightning to prevent a central command from taking control.

investigate.label: Decode the interrupted signal sequence

success.narrate: Nessa recognizes her mentor’s shorthand. The last message names the keystone’s carrier and an unguarded path to the summit.
The log is in a keeper’s private shorthand, and it takes you most of an hour with the station’s codebook. The last message names the keystone’s carrier and an unguarded path to the summit.

investigate.failure: The sequence is broken, but you identify the distress cadence. Someone tried to keep the tower independent.

route.label: Climb beneath the charged signal rings

success.narrate: You earth the lowest ring with the grounding rod and climb through the quiet it leaves, one ring at a time, with the storm hissing on every side. At the top, the control platform is dark and the rain is coming in sideways.

You climb between the strikes, ring by ring, flattening yourselves against the bronze each time the lightning crawls past, with the storm hissing on every side. At the top, the control platform is dark and the rain is coming in sideways.

route.failure: The rings arc across your route. You reach the platform, but the tower’s bound sentinels awaken.

crisis.narrate: The keeper lies under a fallen signal arm, pinned at the leg, with one hand still holding the manual release so the warning keeps going out. She is grey-haired and furious, mostly with the arm.

crisis.text: Don't just stand there. Either lift it or hold the release. Not both. You'll drop one.

crisis.narrate: Behind her, the tower's storm sentinel turns its head of bronze toward you. Its voice comes out of every ring at once.

crisis.text: Surrender the beacon to Central Command. The local keeper is relieved of duty.
The local keeper is not relieved of anything. The local keeper is lying on the floor.

peaceful.label: Transmit the keeper’s independent recall sequence

success.narrate: Wren shouts the old recall sequence up at you from under the arm, a line at a time, and you send it out through the rings: the keeper's own code, the one the tower was built to obey before there was any such thing as Central Command.

The sentinel listens. Then, very slowly, it lowers its head, sets its bronze shoulder under the fallen arm and lifts it, so that you can drag the keeper clear and turn the beacon back toward the road.

success.text: Good. About time somebody remembered whose tower this is.

peaceful.failure: The sentinel recognizes only part of the code. It hesitates long enough for you to reach the manual releases.
peaceful.labelNoLead: Help the trapped keeper send her own recall signal

objective.name: Restore the beacon and free the keeper
objective.label: Reset a beacon release
objective.description: Three successful actions end the encounter. The Storm Grounder also helps these objective checks.
objective.failText: The beacon loses its long-range lens. The keeper still needs release, and some caravans will have to wait for daylight.
objective.successText: The beacon turns toward the road; the keeper’s warning reaches Highpass.

after.narrate: Highpass’s medics carry the keeper down on a door. Her leg is wrong below the knee, and she gives instructions about the beacon the whole way.

after.text: You tied your scarf to the wrong arm. Nobody could see it from the road.
I didn’t tie it. You did. I came because I saw it.
Then I tied it to the wrong arm.

after.narrate: She pushes a folded map into Nessa’s hands: every safe line through the pass, redrawn after each storm for twenty years.

after.text: Reliable as of this morning. After that, it’s yours to keep honest.
I’ll bring it back to you.
Bring it back better.

after.narrate: Before the medics take her down, the keeper, Wren, presses a folded map on you: every safe line through the pass, redrawn after each storm for twenty years. “Give it to someone who’ll keep it honest.”
Highpass asks which travelers should receive the first safe signal windows.

decisions.label: Prioritize the refugee and healer caravans
decisions.text: The most vulnerable travelers reach shelter first. The outpost’s trust grows.

decisions.label: Prioritize supply trains for the whole pass
decisions.text: Food and repair equipment arrive before the next storm front.

signal.approach: The charged rings turn above the climb, throwing sparks onto the rock. The tower’s front stair is open and lit, and every sentinel on the platform can see it.

talks.label: Report to Captain Sorrel

lines.narrate: Captain Sorrel receives you in a storeroom she is using as an office because the office is full of blankets. She is counting something on a slate when you come in and finishes before she looks up.

lines.text: Three hundred and twelve refugees. Two hundred blankets. Eleven beds. One signal tower, shouting for help in a code nobody in this fort can read. I did the sum twice.
The tower keeper is a woman called Wren. She's been up there twenty years. If she's calling for help, it's real. I can't spare a single soldier to go and find out. I can spare you.
Captain.
Stoneward. I heard you were dead.
Not yet.
Good. I haven't got a bed for you either.

summit.name: The Price of a Keystone
summit.threat: Three claimants on a ledge too narrow for a fight, fragile bridges, and somebody who would like to end the argument for everyone. Climbing gear helps travel; knowing what each claimant left out may prevent a fight.
summit.brief: A young courier is carrying the ward keystone over the pass to the shrine at Glasswind. Three parties have promised to protect the region if you hand it to them instead. Find the courier and decide who can be trusted with it.

opening.narrate: The courier is called Bek. He is seventeen, he has been carrying the keystone for a week, and he is sitting on it. Around him, on a ledge too narrow for anybody to start a fight without falling off, three camps are waiting for him to stand up.

Each camp has a banner and a spokesman. Lieutenant Garrow of the Highpass Watch, who wants it kept behind the fort's walls. Factor Tolliver of the Ashford merchant houses, who wants it kept in a bank. And Mother Orla of the Glasswind shrine, where the keepers were meant to meet and name its custodian, who wants it kept there whether they meet or not.

opening.text: I'm not moving. My oath says I take it to whoever the keepers name. Nobody's asked the keepers. Everybody's asked me.
Has anyone fed you?
Mr Tolliver offered. I didn't sign anything.

summit.clue: Each claimant has left one condition out of their offer: the Watch can declare an emergency and take command of it, the merchant houses can sell the custody on, and Glasswind would seal it where no keeper could use it. Bek's oath allows shared custody, witnessed by independent ward keepers.

investigate.label: Compare all three custody agreements

success.narrate: You read all three agreements twice, and then you read out, quietly, to each spokesman in turn, the line they hadn't read out themselves.

The Watch's offer lets the Watch declare an emergency and take command of the stone, and the Watch decides what counts as an emergency. The merchant houses' offer lets them sell the custody on, at a fair market rate. Glasswind's lets the shrine seal it under the mountain, where it is perfectly safe and no keeper can ever use it.
Nobody is humiliated. A common agreement starts to look possible.

failure.narrate: The three agreements blur into one long promise. But Bek, who has had a week to read them, points to the line none of the spokesmen read aloud: custody can be shared.

failure.text: I've been trying to tell them that since Tuesday.

route.label: Secure a neutral meeting place beyond the cracked bridge
route.success: You establish a safe crossing and invite one witness from each camp.
route.failure: A support cracks during the crossing. No one is lost, but accusations fly and hired guards draw weapons.

crisis.narrate: A fourth person steps onto the ledge, and the three camps go quiet. She wears no banner, only a plain grey coat with the badge of Central Command, and she speaks very gently, like someone talking a child down off a roof.

crisis.text: The High Warden sends his regards, and an offer. Bind the stone to one keeper, and the argument ends today. Nobody needs to trust anybody. That's rather the point of it.
No.

crisis.narrate: The agent sighs, as if Bek has said something sad, and reaches for the wrapped stone.

peaceful.label: Bind the claimants to a witnessed shared-custody oath

success.narrate: You put the three agreements down on the rock in front of everybody and ask each spokesman to read their whole agreement aloud, with their own people watching, and strike out anything they would not say in front of them.

Garrow does it first, because he is a soldier and would rather lose quickly. Tolliver does it second, with a face like a man paying a bill. Mother Orla does it last, slowly, and then signs the shared oath under the other two.
With three signatures against her and Bek's oath behind them, the agent has nothing left to command anybody with. She takes her hand back from the stone.

success.text: You'll have the same argument next year. And the year after. We'll still be here.
So will we.

peaceful.failure: Two representatives agree; the third panics as the agent seizes a witness. You must break the coercive seals before anyone is bound.

objective.name: Break the coercive custody seals
objective.label: Release a witness from a binding seal
objective.description: Three successful actions free the witnesses and secure the keystone. Companions cannot negotiate these releases for the hero.
objective.failText: One representative loses trust during the delay. The keystone still needs securing; any custody agreement will begin under strain.
objective.successText: The witnesses stand together and the agent’s seals fall apart.

after.narrate: Bek stands up at last, very stiffly, and hands the keystone to you. He does not let go straight away.

after.text: It's not yours. You know that. You're just carrying it.
That's the only safe way to carry anything.

after.narrate: Who holds the stone from here will shape who answers at the final beacon.

decisions.label: Keep custody shared among the local wards

text.narrate: You carry the keystone, and the local wards share its custody, with one witness from each of the three camps. Bek goes home to sleep for a week.

text.text: If anybody asks, I didn't sit on it the whole time.

decisions.label: Place custody with an accountable regional council

text.narrate: Custody goes to an accountable regional council, with named witnesses and a public record of every hand the stone passes through. Garrow, Tolliver and Orla all sign as witnesses, which none of them enjoys.

summit.approach: A cracked footbridge leads round to a neutral ledge above the three camps. The main path runs straight through all of them, past every banner.

talks.label: Talk to Mother Orla of Glasswind

lines.text: Glasswind has kept the high shrine for four hundred years. We would keep the stone the same way. Safely. Quietly. In the dark, where nobody can use it for anything.
Not even the keepers who need it?
Especially not them. Keepers are how these things go wrong, Sister. Ask Briarwatch.
She means it kindly. That's the frightening part.

talks.label: Talk to Factor Tolliver of Ashford

lines.text: The merchant houses would hold it in trust. Insured. Audited. Every quarter, a statement to every ward on the network. What could be more responsible?
Who pays for the insurance?
Well. The wards. Naturally. Per ring, per year. It's in the schedule.

breach.name: The Quiet District
breach.region: Tallowmarket, the old ward district below Highpass
breach.threat: Iron bell-wardens that walk sleepers back to bed, and evacuation gates locked from the inside. Ward oil and tools help, but the way you lead people out matters most.
breach.brief: Tallowmarket, the old ward district below Highpass, has not sent a messenger in a month. Its people are still there, going about their days, and none of them can choose to leave. Silence the echo-stones that hold them without turning their streets into a battlefield.

opening.narrate: Tallowmarket is very clean. Somebody has swept the steps this morning, and yesterday, and every morning for a month.

Old Hobb the baker kneads an empty board, floured to the elbows, with nothing in the bowl. A girl in a school pinafore opens the school gate, steps through, steps back, and closes it again. Every so often the bell in the square gives a small dry click instead of ringing, and the whole street stops between one breath and the next, and then goes on.

opening.text: That's not sleeping. Sleeping, you get to dream.
They're not unhappy. Listen to them. They're not anything.
Then we don't break anything we can't put back. Not a window.

breach.clue: Three echo-stones replay the district's old routines so that nobody has to decide anything. Break their shared rhythm and the people come back to themselves, without harming the wards that keep the Gloam off the streets.

investigate.label: Find the break between remembered routine and living choice

success.narrate: You kneel by the school gate and ask the girl a question nobody has asked her in a month: what she would do today, if she could do anything.
She stops, with her hand on the latch. Her face does something complicated.

success.text: I'd go and see if Mr Hobb's got any crusts. And then... there's three stones. Under the clock, the chapel and the well. They hum. I don't like them.

success.narrate: Then the bell clicks, and she opens the gate again. But you know where to go.

failure.narrate: Your questions slide off them. But Maren, standing in the square with her eyes shut, counts the pauses against the clock tower and frowns.

failure.text: They're not stopping on the hour. They're stopping when something tells them to. It's not in them. It's coming from outside.

route.label: Reach the echo-stones through the service courtyards

success.narrate: You move through the back courtyards behind the routines, where everyone is too busy doing what they did yesterday to see you. Orin wedges the evacuation gate with a bread paddle from Hobb's yard before anything thinks to lock it.

failure.narrate: A service door bangs against the path of a bell-warden on its rounds. Iron feet turn towards you down the alley. But the evacuation gate is close, and it is still open.

crisis.narrate: In the square the magistrate is waiting for you: Magistrate Imelda Rook, in her chain of office, standing very straight under the clicking bell. Beside her stands the tallest of the iron bell-wardens, with her face cast in its bronze. When it speaks, it speaks in her voice, and every echo-stone in the district speaks with it.

crisis.text: Residents are to remain indoors for their safety. The Gloam is near. The wards are holding. Nobody needs to go anywhere. Nobody needs to decide.

crisis.narrate: Then, under it, so quietly you nearly miss it, her own voice.

crisis.text: Don't break the wards. Please. The mist is right there, past the wall. Get them out, but don't break the wards.

crisis.narrate: The iron bell-wardens step out of their doorways, polite as ushers, to walk everyone safely home.

peaceful.label: Give the residents a new, voluntary signal to follow

success.narrate: Nessa starts it, because somebody has to: a skipping song from the road, the first one she ever learned. Maren takes up the tune from the next window. Then, from his doorway, very hoarse, Old Hobb.
Maren starts it, because somebody has to: a hymn from the shrine at home, sung badly. Orin takes up the tune from the next window. Then, from his doorway, very hoarse, Old Hobb.

It is not a routine. Nobody in Tallowmarket has heard it before. One by one, all down the street, people stop what they did yesterday and choose to answer it, and the voice in the bell runs out of mouths to borrow.

failure.narrate: A handful of people wake, blinking in their doorways. It is enough to start getting them out. It is not enough to stop the bell, which tightens its hold on everyone else and sends the bell-wardens after you.

objective.name: Silence the echo-stones without breaking the wards
objective.label: Silence an echo-stone
objective.description: Four successful actions free the district. Finish before round seven to keep all three of Tallowmarket's wards standing.
objective.failText: The last echo-stone burns out one of the district's wards on its way down. Tallowmarket still needs freeing, and somebody will have to rebuild that ward before winter.
objective.successText: The last stone goes quiet. All down the street people begin to make small, uncertain choices of their own. Old Hobb sits down on his step and cries, and then gets up and asks who has any flour.

after.narrate: Magistrate Rook takes her chain of office off and holds it in both hands, as if it has got heavier.

after.text: The wards did that to us for our own good. They did keep the mist out. I want you to understand that. Nobody here was hurt.
So you tell me. When is a ward allowed to overrule the people it's guarding? Because somebody is going to ask the next town that question, and I'd like the answer written down before they do.

after.narrate: Whatever you answer, it will go with you to the first beacon.

decisions.label: Require the keeper’s and community’s consent

text.narrate: Tallowmarket adopts a double-consent rule: a ward may only hold people with its keeper's word and the district's together, and either can take it back. Rook writes it on the wall of the square in whitewash, where the bell can read it.

decisions.label: Create a public emergency oversight council

text.narrate: Tallowmarket sets up a public oversight council. Emergency powers need named votes, a record anyone can read, and a date when they run out. Old Hobb is elected first, because he was the first to choose anything for himself.

breach.approach: The service courtyards run behind the bakery and the school, where the routines are loudest. The main street is empty except for the clicking, and the iron bell-wardens walking their rounds.

talks.label: Talk to Old Hobb the baker

lines.narrate: Hobb does not stop kneading. But when you ask him what he is making, his hands slow, as if the question has caught on something.

lines.text: Bread. For the morning. I always... the morning's when they come in. Posy from the school, she has the end crust.
There's no flour. Did I say? There's been no flour for... it doesn't matter. The bell says it doesn't matter. It's very kind about it.

lines.narrate: The bell clicks. Hobb's face smooths out like a sheet, and his hands go on kneading the empty board.

lines.text: He knew. For a moment he knew. That's the thread we pull.

beacon.name: The Chorus at Dawn
beacon.threat: The iron chorus at the first beacon, guarded by bound echoes. The keystone, your friends, and the choices you made on the road decide how it can be stopped.
beacon.brief: Central Command is preparing its final signal. Carry the keystone to the first beacon, and decide whether the ward network will be a shield shared by many people or a command held by one.

opening.narrate: The first beacon stands above the cloud line, on a stair cut into the mountain before anyone now alive was born. Its bronze rings are open to the sky, and something is singing in them.

Every so often you catch a voice you know. Old Hobb. Captain Sorrel. Brannagh, who barely said a word to you in Fenmere, saying one now. Each one is cut off after one word, filed down to a single obedient note, and fitted into the chorus with the rest.

opening.text: That's everyone we've met.
That's everyone we've helped. It's learned them from the wards we mended.
Then we know the words better than it does.

beacon.clue: The iron chorus has no voice of its own: only the borrowed ones. Let the wards answer for themselves and it falls apart. Or break it by force, and burn the great lens with it.

investigate.label: Listen for the separate voices beneath the command

success.narrate: You stop trying to hear the chorus and listen for the people inside it instead. Each one, once you know them, is a little off the beat.
The drivers you paid back are in there, every family still keeping its own count, and no two counts the same.
The sluice-house keepers are in there, still bickering about who opens which gate. The council you left in the marsh has never once agreed on time.
The demolition crew from the bridge are in there, singing a work song they learned beside the refugees, and none of them can carry a tune.
Their choices on the road give you a rhythm the chorus cannot predict, because nobody chose it for them.

failure.narrate: The chorus swallows you whole. But one by one your companions each pick out a voice they know, and hold onto it, and you can follow them to the keystone cradle.

route.label: Carry the keystone through the resonant rings

success.narrate: You earth the nearest rings with the grounding rod, as you did on Wren's tower, and climb through the quiet patch it leaves. You reach the cradle before the chorus has finished tuning them.
You time your climb between the peals, a ring at a time, the way Wren's tower taught you, and reach the cradle before the chorus has finished tuning them.

failure.narrate: A peal goes through the stair like a hammer through a plate, and the whole party is thrown against the stone. The cradle is still in reach. But the bound echoes have gathered round it, waiting.

crisis.narrate: The rings close into one note, and the note finds words. The voice is a man’s: tired, patient, and very reasonable.

crisis.text: High Warden Corvane, Central Command. You have walked a long way to break the only thing that has ever kept the Gloam out of a nursery.

I have watched councils. I watched one argue about whose turn it was to ring the bell while the mist came over the wall. The vote was still open when the last house went quiet. The design you are standing in was drawn by someone who saw that. She wanted a voice that could answer before the arguing finished. So do I.
And who does the voice answer to?
Nobody needs to. That is the point, Stoneward.
He believes it. Every word.

crisis.narrate: The Single Voice offers perfect safety, and asks only for every keeper's choice in return. It would have sounded better before Tallowmarket. You have seen what that kind of safety looks like from the inside: a clean street, and a man kneading bread with no flour.

peaceful.label: Ask the independent keepers to answer together

success.narrate: You set the keystone in its cradle and do not tell it anything. Instead you call the keepers, one at a time, by name: the ones you met, the ones on Maren's list, the ones who were never asked.

They answer in different rhythms, out of time with each other and badly out of tune. The chorus cannot make them agree without choosing for them, and the moment it tries to choose, the note it has been holding all year comes apart in its hands.

success.text: Listen to that. It's dreadful. It's wonderful.

failure.narrate: The first voices answer, and then falter under the weight of the note. Your companions put their backs to the cradle and hold the echoes off while you open the rest, one channel at a time.

objective.name: Restore a chorus of independent wards
objective.label: Open an independent ward channel
objective.description: Four successful actions break the iron chorus. Choices you made earlier on the road lower the difficulty, and the change is shown before you roll.
objective.failText: The great lens cracks with the chorus still singing in it. Break the chorus to free the roads; mending the lens will take years.
objective.successText: Separate voices fill the rings, all out of step. The region's wards become a chorus, not a chain.

after.narrate: Dawn comes up over the cloud and goes down the mountain to the roads, one village at a time. Somewhere below, a bell rings properly, then another, nowhere near in time.

after.text: That's the worst bell-ringing I've ever heard.
That's all of them. Ringing for themselves.

after.narrate: Your party has earned the right to say what its strength is for. Back in Highpass, the guild has prepared the first advancement trial. Not a reward for obedience, but a question.

decisions.label: Leave the wards in independent, cooperating hands

text.narrate: Every settlement keeps its own voice and its own keeper. Your party becomes the road between them, not a throne above them. Nobody will ever be told what to do by the first beacon again. They will have to argue instead.

decisions.label: Found a public charter for the ward network

text.narrate: A public charter for the ward network: what it may do, what it may never do, and the names of the people who must answer when it is used. It is nailed to the beacon door. Within a week somebody has written a complaint in the margin.

beacon.approach: The rings hum between you and the keystone cradle, close enough to feel in your teeth. The pilgrims’ stair goes straight up the middle, where the command will hear every step.

talks.label: Stop on the stair and talk

lines.narrate: At the foot of the stair, you all stop at once without anybody saying so. The keystone is warm through its wrappings.

lines.text: Before we go up. If it goes wrong up there, I take the front. That's not a discussion.
If it goes wrong up there, I'm running. Just so everyone knows. Towards it, probably. But running.
Whatever's at the top, it thinks it's right. Somebody built it because they were frightened. Don't forget that when you're angry with it.
And don't forget the angry part either.

trial.name: Oath of the Road — First Advancement
trial.threat: A supervised trial of judgment and technique. Failure has no gold penalty and can be retried; your class mastery cannot be lost to one bad roll.
trial.brief: Show how you use your strength when victory and protection compete. Complete this trial to earn your class mastery. Your next branch, your second job, is chosen at level 20.
trial.opening: The trainers create an echo of the road you have traveled. Your companions stand beside you; behind a fragile gate, voices ask whether your next step will leave them behind.
trial.clue: The trial’s gate responds to commitment, not brute force. A deliberate choice of responsibility can resolve the echo without defeating it.

investigate.label: Discuss what the road taught you with your companions

success.narrate: The trainers dim the echo and leave you the bench by the gate. Nobody hurries you.

success.text: At Ashford you let the bridge crews work off what they owed instead of hanging it on them. I wanted a tribunal. I was wrong, and the bridge got mended in half the time.
At Ashford you kept Hal’s orders and called a tribunal. Slow. But every carter on that bridge watched it happen, and none of them had to take our word for anything.
You gave the diagram to every keeper who asked. Some of them will use it badly. All of them can use it.
You put the diagram where it could be watched, with a name beside every copy. I wrote the names down too. Habit.
Highpass. You sent the refugee carts through first, and the supply train sat in the snow a whole day. I counted the people on those carts. Forty-two.
Highpass. You sent the supply trains first. I was angry for a week. Then the pass had food all winter, and I stopped being angry and started being annoyed that you were right.

success.narrate: Each of them is holding a different day of the road. Between them, the trial’s question gets smaller and sharper: not what you can do, but who you do it for.

failure.narrate: The trainers leave you the bench by the gate. It goes badly.

failure.text: The Quiet District. Double consent. If a ward has to ask twice before it saves someone, someone drowns while it’s asking.
And if it never has to ask, you get a street full of bakers kneading empty boards.
That’s not fair.
It isn’t meant to be fair. It’s meant to be true.
The oversight council. Named votes, a fixed expiry. I like it. I like anything with an expiry.
You like it because it sounds like a duty roster. Councils lie in ways a roster can’t.
Name one.
Every council I have ever sat on.

failure.narrate: Nobody wins. But by the end you know what each of them is afraid you might become, and that is its own kind of answer.

route.label: Demonstrate your class technique on the approach
route.success: The trainers recognize a practiced technique used for a purpose. The gate responds.
route.failure: The technique falters, and a trainer resets the echo. You learn from the miss and proceed without losing your path.

trial.crisis: The echo offers an easy victory while the gate behind it cracks. The trainers watch whether you pursue the enemy or take responsibility for the people in your care.

peaceful.label: Name your responsibility and let the easy victory go
peaceful.success: You refuse the false choice. The echo bows and the gate opens; the trial recognizes your judgment.
peaceful.failure: The words are not enough. The trainers ask you to show the decision while the echo presses its attack.

objective.name: Demonstrate responsibility under pressure
objective.label: Secure the trial gate
objective.description: Three successful actions complete the demonstration. A failed trial is recoverable and cannot permanently lock an advancement.
objective.failText: The trainers mark the missed deadline for discussion. Finish the demonstration or withdraw and retry; your advancement cannot be permanently lost.
objective.successText: The gate holds. The trainers acknowledge the intent behind your technique.

after.narrate: The echo is gone. The gate is still standing, and so are the people behind it. The trainers wait with the guild’s book open. The Oath of the Road is one sentence long, and they will not say it for you.

after.text: They want it out loud. I said mine to a sergeant with a head cold. Don’t overthink it.
Overthink it a little. Then mean it.
Or say it fast, before you can change your mind. That’s what I’d do.
That is what you’d do.

decisions.label: Swear the Oath of the Road: for the people who cannot hold the road themselves
decisions.description: Speak your oath. The guild records it, and the road remembers it. Every oath earns the same class mastery.

text.narrate: “I will hold the road for the people who cannot hold it themselves, and I will not leave them behind to win.”

text.text: Good.

text.narrate: The guild writes it down. Your second job is chosen at level 20. A relief convoy is stuck on the Highpass road and needs you now; the practice arena stays open for safe experiments.

decisions.label: Swear the Oath of the Road: for the ones who walk it with you
decisions.description: Speak your oath. The guild records it, and the road remembers it. Every oath earns the same class mastery.

text.narrate: “I will walk the road with the people beside me, and I will not ask them to go where I will not.”

text.text: You already don’t. You just never said it.

text.narrate: The guild writes it down. Your second job is chosen at level 20. A relief convoy is stuck on the Highpass road and needs you now; the practice arena stays open for safe experiments.

decisions.label: Swear the Oath of the Road: for the towns, even when they cannot agree
decisions.description: Speak your oath. The guild records it, and the road remembers it. Every oath earns the same class mastery.

text.narrate: “I will keep the road open for every town on it, and I will not choose which of them is worth saving.”

text.text: Even Fenmere?

text.narrate: “Especially Fenmere.”
The guild writes it down. Your second job is chosen at level 20. A relief convoy is stuck on the Highpass road and needs you now; the practice arena stays open for safe experiments.

trial.approach: The trainers have laid out the echo’s road: a course built to show your technique, and beside it a plain path straight to the gate. Either is allowed. Both are watched.

aftermath.name: The Road You Keep
aftermath.threat: One of the iron chorus's last bell-wardens is holding a relief caravan at a gate. Ward Oil can affect its guards; a climbing kit reaches the emergency channel above the gate.
aftermath.brief: Take your new mastery onto the road. A bell-warden left over from the iron chorus has mistaken a relief convoy for an invading army, and the first free towns need the convoy's medicine.

opening.narrate: Children have painted the convoy's crates with the signs of their towns. Ahead, at a gate of pale metal, a tall iron bell-warden is repeating an evacuation order that has been out of date since the beacon fell. Nobody told it. Nobody was left whose job it was to tell it.
The lead driver, a broad woman called Oda, has stopped arguing with it and started counting the sick.

aftermath.clue: The bell-warden still accepts the old roadwardens' oath of responsibility. Its own emergency channel can open the gate without waking anything else that answered to the chorus.

investigate.label: Read the obsolete evacuation orders with the drivers
investigate.success: The contradictory commands reveal an emergency channel. It was designed for a keeper who would take personal responsibility for admitting the convoy.
investigate.failure: The exact wording is damaged, but the drivers remember a keeper’s oath. You know enough to challenge its orders, though not how to make it easy.

route.label: Reach the emergency channel above the gate
route.success: The party reaches the channel before the guards can close the gallery. Your new training makes the opening feel usable, not merely lucky.
route.failure: A guard breaks the gallery brace. The party reaches the channel with injuries and without surprise.

aftermath.crisis: The bell-warden asks who will answer for the people beyond its gate. Its guards advance. You may offer a binding promise, disable the bell-warden, or work the channel while your companions keep the road open.

peaceful.label: Take responsibility for the convoy under the keepers’ oath

success.narrate: The bell-warden asks for a keeper who will answer for the people beyond its gate. You have already sworn to something like that, out loud, in front of witnesses.
You give it the words you gave the guild: the people who cannot hold the road themselves.
You give it the words you gave the guild: the ones who walk the road with you, and the convoy is walking it now.
You give it the words you gave the guild: every town on the road, even the ones that cannot agree.
The bell-warden accepts a responsible keeper in place of a distant master. It opens the gate and records the convoy’s destination, not its obedience.

peaceful.failure: The damaged bell-warden refuses the oath. You must make room for the convoy before its guards enforce the old order.

objective.name: Open the relief convoy’s route
objective.label: Release an emergency road channel
objective.description: Four successful actions open the gate. Your new class mastery is among your combat actions: use it to buy whoever works the channel the time they need.
objective.failText: The convoy loses a day’s supply while it waits. Open the road to get the medicine through; the delay will be remembered.
objective.successText: The convoy passes between lowered weapons. People see what your new title means before anyone announces it.

after.narrate: The convoy reaches the first settlement before dusk. Your mastery has faced something more demanding than a title ceremony: people depending on the way you choose to act.
The drivers have news from over the mountains. High Warden Corvane has gone home to Vell. Nobody on the convoy knows what he will do there. Nobody is sorry he has gone.

decisions.label: Leave local keepers in charge of the road

text.narrate: The convoy appoints a keeper from each town. Your party leaves a working agreement rather than another command.

On the road home a rider in Highpass colours meets the convoy. The towns are sending delegates to Highpass, and the first council of the free wards sits at the end of the week. Captain Sorrel wants your party there. She did not say why, which from Sorrel means she expects trouble.

decisions.label: Found a voluntary road patrol with the companions

text.narrate: Your companions help volunteers agree on duties they can refuse or revise. The road belongs to those who keep it open.

On the road home a rider in Highpass colours meets the convoy. The towns are sending delegates to Highpass, and the first council of the free wards sits at the end of the week. Captain Sorrel wants your party there. She did not say why, which from Sorrel means she expects trouble.

approach.narrate: The emergency channel sits in a gallery above the gate, reached by a service ladder the guards have half pulled up. Below, the driver has laid the sick out in the shade of the crates, in order of who can wait least.

approach.text: Whatever you’re going to do, do it before the shade moves.

approach.narrate: Battle Surge is fresh in your arms. One breath of it would carry you up that ladder through a guard’s swing, and make your next blow land true.
Vanishing Step would put you in the gallery’s shadows before the guards had finished turning round.
An Arcane Barrier over whoever climbs first would let them take a guard’s blow and keep working.
Divine Aegis can keep whoever holds the channel on their feet while the guards try to drag them off it.
From the top of a crate, one Volley would reach every guard on the gallery at once.
Song of Rest will not open a gate, but it will keep the whole party standing while you do.

chairs.name: The Chair Problem
chairs.region: The officers' mess at Highpass Watch
chairs.threat: A council that cannot agree on its seating, and a Gloam front climbing the lower pass toward the refugee camp. Highpass's ward will only ring at full strength if the delegates agree to share its charge.
chairs.brief: The first council of the free wards sits at Highpass. Fenmere has sent for help. Get the towns to agree on anything before the mist does it for them.

opening.narrate: The first council of the free wards meets in the officers' mess at Highpass, because it is the only room in the fort with enough chairs. It does not have enough chairs.

opening.text: Six delegates. Five good chairs. One that rocks. I did the sum twice.

opening.narrate: Reeve Aveline has come for Briarwatch with a satchel of lists and the face of a woman who has not slept since the bell went quiet. Quartermaster Iona is here for Ashford, already reading the room's lease. Brannagh has come up from Fenmere, white-haired, in a mud-stiff cloak, with the same brown goat on a rope. She nods to you once, which from her is a long conversation. Nobody has asked about the goat.

On the door is Lieutenant Garrow of the Watch, who stood witness for the Watch when the keystone's custody was shared on the summit ledge. He nods to you the way people nod at someone they have signed something with.

On the door is Lieutenant Garrow of the Watch, who signed as a witness when the keystone went to the regional council. He carries his copy of the custody record inside his coat, in case anybody asks. Nobody has.
And there is the delegate from Merrowgate: Provost Elske Marrow, grey-eyed, ink on two fingers, with a guild clerk at her elbow who writes down everything, including the weather.

opening.text: Ashford will not sit below Merrowgate. Not on the first day. It sets a precedent.
Below? It's a table, Iona. It doesn't have a below.
It has a head, Reeve. Heads have a below.

opening.narrate: Sorrel, who has had the morning she was expecting, points at Orin.

opening.text: Stoneward. You're sergeant at arms. Keep order.
Understood.

opening.narrate: Orin takes the job the way he takes every job. Within the hour he has collected two belt knives, a letter-opener and the bread knife, which he returns to the cook with an apology and a receipt. He stops at the goat.

opening.text: Madam. Does she bite?
Only Ashford.

opening.narrate: Across the room, Iona does not look up from her papers. She and the goat have shared a room for two nights now, and neither of them has forgiven the other.

At midday Elske Marrow takes the seating chart off the wall, turns it over and draws a circle. Order of arrival. Merrowgate, which arrived first, she puts last. It takes her five minutes, and nobody can find anything wrong with it, which annoys Iona more than the head of the table did.

opening.text: There. Now that the furniture is settled, Fenmere's delegate has something to say. She has been waiting since breakfast.
Since the day before yesterday. Fenmere sent for help three days ago. The mist is in our lower fields. This is the meeting I sent for.

opening.narrate: The council spends the afternoon on who should pay for it.

opening.text: Every one of them means what they say. That is the trouble.
Can't we just go? Fenmere's two days east. We could be halfway.
Without supplies or a road warrant. We'd arrive as six more mouths.

talks.label: Ask Provost Marrow why she gave Merrowgate the last seat

lines.narrate: Elske is on the wall walk, looking down at the refugee camp in the lower pass. She does not turn around.

lines.text: Because the last seat speaks last, and by then everyone is tired of talking. People mistake that for modesty.
You broke the Single Voice. Good. Corvane turned it into a fist. It was meant to be a hand.

lines.narrate: She says it the way people say the name of a house they used to live in.

lines.text: You knew its design.
I drew it, Sister. A long time ago, for a town that no longer exists. I'll tell you about it when there is time, and there is never time. That is rather my point.
She's telling the truth. All of it, as far as I can hear.

talks.label: Sit with Brannagh of Fenmere and her goat

lines.narrate: Brannagh has taken the rocking chair without complaint and is eating an apple in very small, very deliberate bites. The goat is eating the core of the last one.

lines.text: Sit down. You make the room look busy.

Fenmere has two halves. The upper village on the rise, the lower village by the water. The mist came into the lower fields four days ago. Our keeper says the ward will hold the lower village a week. Our keeper is an optimist. I've told her so.

You've been to Fenmere before. The bitter water at the sluice. You left us a water council, one keeper for each bank, and I'm the village side. We've argued every week since, and the water has never been cleaner. That's what I'd like from this lot.
You've been to Fenmere before. The bitter water at the sluice. Ashford's engineers still come out every month to look at the sluice, and send us the bill. Ashford is very reliable about bills.
What's the goat's name?
She's with me.

lines.narrate: That appears to be all the answer there is going to be.

lines.text: Get them to say yes to something before dark. Anything. Once a council has said yes once, it gets the taste for it.

talks.label: Ask Aveline how she is holding up

lines.text: Fine. Busy. I have the Briarwatch grain figures, the Briarwatch roof figures and a letter from Tovin asking whether his apprentice may ring the practice bell at night. The answer is no. I've written it three times.
When did you last sleep?
I slept on the cart.
You did the grain figures on the cart. I watched you.

lines.narrate: Aveline looks at her satchel as if it has betrayed her.

lines.text: When this council has agreed on one thing, Stoneward, I will sleep for a week. Help me get it there.

chairs.clue: Every delegate is waiting for someone else to pay first, because whoever pays for Fenmere today pays for every town tomorrow. Highpass's own ward can only ring at full strength with all five towns' consent: the charter you left at the beacon, or the custom of the independent keepers, makes it so.

investigate.label: Find out what is really stopping the vote

success.narrate: By late afternoon you can name the knot. Ashford will pay if Merrowgate pays. Merrowgate will pay if the money is a loan. Highpass will pay in soldiers, not coin, and has no soldiers to spare. Nobody is lying. Everybody is afraid of being the first.

success.text: Off the record? If I say yes today, my guild makes me pay for every washed-out bridge from here to the sea. I'll say yes. I need someone else to say it first.

investigate.failure: The arguments go round so many times you lose the thread, but you notice who is watching whom. Each delegate is waiting for someone else to commit first.

route.label: Take the cliff path down to the lower gate
route.success: You go down the cliff path instead of the switchbacks and reach the lower gate while the mist is still in the trees. The wardens on the gate have time to hear what you need from them.
route.failure: The switchbacks are jammed with people coming up and carts going down. You get to the lower gate bruised and late, as the first cold touches the palisade.

direct.label: Go down the switchbacks with everyone else
direct.text: You go down the switchbacks in the crush, with carts going down and people coming up, and reach the lower gate together, late, as the cold touches the palisade.

approach.narrate: The bell in the watchtower starts to ring the alarm just before sunset. Not the ward. The ordinary alarm, a hand-bell, swung by somebody who has run out of better ideas.

approach.text: Mist in the lower pass. It followed the Fenmere rider up the valley. The camp's below the line of the ward.

approach.narrate: The ward itself hangs in Highpass's gate arch, and it is answering the mist in a thin, uncertain voice.
Since the beacon, no single keeper may ring it to full strength alone. The charter you nailed to the beacon door says so, and somebody has already written a complaint about it in the margin.

Since the beacon, no single keeper may ring it to full strength alone. Nobody wrote that down. The keepers agreed it among themselves, after the beacon, and they have kept to it, which is more than most written rules manage.

approach.text: Don't look at me like that. I'm coming.

crisis.narrate: The Gloam comes up the lower pass like a tide coming in over flat sand: quietly, faster than it looks. Where it touches the palisade the wood greys and goes soft, and the frost on it forms in the shapes of things that were there earlier: a cart, a fire, a child's hopscotch squares. Shapes come out of it with it. Not quite people. What the mist has taken, walking.

crisis.text: Wall's no good against that. The ward is.

crisis.narrate: Up in the gate arch the Highpass ward is ringing at a third of its strength. To ring it fully, the delegates who followed you down must say together that they consent. Elske is already beside the bell-rope. Iona is at the back, and Brannagh is between them with the goat.

crisis.text: This is what I meant. Five people must agree before a bell may ring. Tell them quickly.

peaceful.label: Get the five delegates to consent, here and now

success.text: Fenmere consents. First, if anybody's counting.
Ashford consents. Second. Somebody write it down.

success.narrate: Aveline, Sorrel and Elske say it together. The ward catches the five voices and rings with all of them, and the note goes down the pass like a wave pushing back the tide. The shapes in the mist come apart into frost, and the frost melts.

success.text: Agreed in under a minute. When the alternative is dying, councils are wonderfully efficient.

failure.text: I can't commit Ashford on a bell-rope. I need it in writing.
Then write fast.

failure.narrate: The ward rings at half strength. It is not enough. The shapes come over the palisade, and you have to hold the gate while the delegates find their words.

objective.name: Hold the lower gate until the ward rings
objective.label: Hold the gate and give the delegates time
objective.description: Four successful actions hold the gate long enough for the five delegates to consent and the ward to ring at full strength.
objective.failText: The mist reaches the first tents before the ward rings. The people escape uphill; their tents, their bedding and some of what they remembered do not.
objective.successText: Five voices answer together. The ward rings at full strength and the pass clears from the top down.

after.narrate: Afterwards the council goes back up to the mess, where the chairs are exactly as they were. Somebody has found a sixth one.

after.text: Well. We agreed on something.
Well. We agreed on something.
We did. Can we agree on another thing before I fall over?
We did. Can we agree on another thing before I fall over?
Well. We didn't agree on anything, and we're all still alive. At my age you take what you're given.
Then let's agree on one thing before I fall over.

after.narrate: Elske Marrow stays standing.

after.text: Fenmere's help leaves at first light. It should have left three days ago. I'll say it once and then I'll stop: a council that needs a mist at the door to agree on anything will always agree one day late. When the council sits again, Merrowgate will make a proposal. I'd like you all to read it before you hate it.

after.narrate: Then the room argues, for the last time today, about who pays for Fenmere.

decisions.label: Back Brannagh: each town pays by what it has to lose

text.text: Big towns lose more, big towns pay more. My goat could work that out.

text.narrate: Iona does the sum, scowls, and signs. The council has its first agreement on paper. It took eleven hours and a mist.

decisions.label: Take Merrowgate's offer: the lantern guilds lend the money

text.narrate: Elske's clerk produces the loan papers before anyone has finished asking for them. They are generous, well drafted and signed in advance by Guildmaster Pell Haverick of the Merrowgate lantern guilds, who is not in the room.

text.text: Who's Haverick?
The man who pays for my lamps. He likes to be useful.

decisions.label: Pledge your contract fee to start Fenmere's relief tonight
decisions.description: This decision is permanent. The council repays your pledge from the relief fund once it is agreed, so your reward is unchanged; the story remembers who paid first.

text.narrate: You put your contract fee on the table, as a pledge, so the first carts can leave tonight. It is not enough for a week, but it is enough for a day, and the room goes very quiet.

text.text: That's not how councils work.
It is now. Ashford, you're embarrassed. Pay the rest.

text.narrate: Iona pays the rest. Later the relief fund pays back your pledge to the penny, and Iona sends you a receipt for it, very correctly made out, with a note on the back that just says: noted.

fenmere.name: Fenmere Under the Gloam
fenmere.region: Fenmere, two days east of Highpass
fenmere.threat: The Gloam has taken Fenmere's lower village and is climbing toward the upper village on the rise. Floodwater runs ahead of it. Bring light; a rope helps on the causeway.
fenmere.brief: The council's help reaches Fenmere a day late. The lower village is gone. Get its people up the rise and keep the upper village from going the same way.

opening.narrate: You come over the last fell at noon and see Fenmere the way the crows see it. The upper village sits on its rise, chimneys smoking. Below it, where Brannagh said the lower village would be, there is a white field, perfectly flat, perfectly still. The roofs are under it. There is no sound at all.

opening.text: That's the lower village.

opening.narrate: She says it the way she would say the name of a neighbour. Then she starts down the hill, and you have to hurry to keep up with a woman of seventy and her goat.

On the rise, the people of the lower village are sitting on their bundles in the churchyard: three hundred of them, give or take. They got out. They got out with what they could carry, two nights ago, while the council was arguing about chairs. Some of them are already looking at the white field as if they can't quite remember what was under it.

opening.text: That's the Gloam's work. It takes the warmth first, then the memory.
How long since the ward went quiet?

Since this morning. You remember me, from the sluice-house. I'm still the keeper. I was ringing it all night, and then I couldn't remember the third verse. I can't remember it now. I've known it since I was nine.

The ward went quiet this morning. You remember me, from the sluice-house. I'm still the keeper. I was ringing it all night, and then I couldn't remember the third verse. I can't remember it now. I've known it since I was nine.

talks.label: Go with Brannagh to look at the lower village

lines.narrate: Brannagh stands at the edge of the white and looks at a place about a hundred yards in, where a weathervane sticks up out of the mist at a slant.

lines.text: That's my roof. Forty years. I re-thatched it in spring. Paid a man from Ashford, and he did it badly, and I made him do it again.

lines.narrate: She does not cry. She does not do anything. After a while the goat leans against her leg and she puts a hand on its head.

lines.text: Three days. If help had come in three days, the ward would have held. Ilka would still have her verse. Write that down somewhere, would you? Somebody should.

talks.label: Ask the lower-village families what the mist has taken from them

lines.narrate: A man knows his daughter's face but not her name. He keeps starting to say it. A woman remembers her house in every detail except which door was hers. A boy of about eight has forgotten he was afraid of the dark, and keeps walking toward the white field to see what's in it.

lines.text: It will come back to most of them, if the mist goes back down. Not all. Not all of it.
I've got him.

lines.narrate: Nessa has the boy by the back of his collar. She sits him down beside Biscuit and tells him the dog's whole history, most of it invented, and he stays.

fenmere.clue: Fenmere's ward is a song in four verses. Ilka has lost the third, but the villagers each remember a piece of it: the lower village sang it at weddings. Rung with the whole song, the ward can push the Gloam back off the rise, though not out of the lower village.

investigate.label: Help Ilka find the third verse among the villagers
